shots.phrase: Begin by framing Program Overview and Status as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
When registered for co-op, students are considered by RIT to have full-time status.
List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion.
Now define Time Commitment Requirements precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
In order to register for co-op for either fall or spring semester, we expect that students will work a minimum of 14 weeks and work a minimum of 35 hours per week.
Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them.
With the foundation in place, examine how Prerequisite Coursework operates in a concrete sequence.
Students must complete a student co-op work report for each term for which they are registered; students are also evaluated each term by their supervisor.
Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition.
Next, compare the choices involved in Student Work Report Requirement and make the decision criteria explicit.

A satisfactory grade is given for co-op when both a completed student co-op work report and a completed, corresponding supervisor evaluation are received and when both documents are generally consistent.
Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts.
Apply Supervisor Evaluation Requirement to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Consider this worked case: A supervisor reviews the student's code commits and deliverables to provide a formal performance evaluation.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Grading Consistency Standard, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate.
State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable.
Stress-test the reasoning around Ethical Computing Principles with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Responsible Research Communication to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Research Integrity and Transparency to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Limitations and threats to validity should be made visible.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice.
For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step.
